title: Standard input and output: data contracts and a verifiable project
lead: Handle valid and malformed input, inspect a remaining newline, and finish the module with an exact file-transfer calculation.
why: Programs receive character streams rather than prevalidated numbers. A reliable interface separates parsing, domain range, and extra data while preserving reproducible output. Nexus’s finite stdin field makes this convenient but differs from a live terminal.
objectives: Read numbers with cin and check success before use.
Distinguish fail, eof, empty input, and a line ending.
Explain std::string, getline, and std::ws behavior.
Use fixed/setprecision without claiming exact internal double representation.
Implement a strict contract, prove integer bounds, and preserve a project test report.
prerequisites: All previous Module 2 lessons, simple if/else, and early return from Module 1.
Integer division, early long long multiplication, comparisons, bool, references, and live objects. No loops or authored functions are needed.

concepts.definition: Standard input. Nexus supplies a finite character sequence followed by end of input.
Reading a typed value with >> according to parsing and stream-state rules.
Reports failed extraction or a more serious error; a value after failure is not treated as validated input.
Reports end of input already encountered rather than predicting future extraction success.
A library type for a sequence of characters; string algorithms are studied separately.
Reads through a delimiter, usually newline; the delimiter is extracted but not included in the result.
Consumes leading whitespace, including newlines and blank lines, up to a nonwhitespace character or end of input.

sections.title: Session 1. Reading is an operation with a result
paragraphs: std::cin >> count attempts to parse an int into an existing object. >> here extracts from a stream rather than shifting bits. Normal formatted extraction skips leading whitespace. cin >> a >> b extracts sequentially but may fail before reading the second value.

if (!(std::cin >> count)) checks failure of the operation. In this condition the stream indicates whether its post-read state is usable; ! negates that result. On failure we print invalid and return before using the number. Parsing success does not establish the domain range, which requires a separate check.

sections.title: A line ending is not end of input
paragraphs: Nexus supplies stdin as a finite buffer. After its last character, extraction can encounter EOF, end of input. In a live terminal, Enter normally adds a newline without closing the stream; more input may still arrive. A strict whole-tail check using ws can therefore wait for end of input in a live terminal.

eof() reports an already-set state, not whether another number exists. Do not replace extraction checks with while(!cin.eof()). Our finite-input task checks the actual extraction first and then, after ws, rejects a nonwhitespace tail.

sections.title: Stream state and evidence-based rejection
paragraphs: fail() reports failed reading or bad state; eof() reports an encountered end. Both can be true when reading a number from an empty buffer. Successfully extracting the final number without trailing whitespace can set eof without an extraction failure. Thus eof alone does not mean an invalid number.

We stop processing on error here. Recovery with clear and discarding damaged input needs a separate policy and usually a loop; it is not a hidden requirement. An input number too large for long long must cause extraction failure rather than become trusted calculation data.

sections.title: Session 2. Strings, remaining delimiters, and getline
paragraphs: <string> supplies std::string, a ready-made text type. std::string line; starts empty. std::getline(std::cin, line) stores characters before the newline and consumes the newline itself. After cin >> count that newline often remains, so the next getline can successfully obtain an empty line.

std::getline(std::cin >> std::ws, name) first removes all leading whitespace, then reads text. It suits a name without significant leading spaces but destroys blank lines and indentation. Do not use it when an empty line is meaningful data. The comma separates arguments to a library function; no authored functions are required.

sections.title: A strict numeric contract and its tail
paragraphs: Integer extraction can successfully read the initial 8 in 8.5 and leave .5. Extraction success alone therefore does not prove that the entire input contains exactly the required integer fields. After all fields, use cin >> ws and check eof(): .5 or extra remains and is rejected. A whitespace-only tail is permitted.

The task uses the environment’s ordinary numeric format without changing locale. A C++ source literal 010 was octal; stdin text follows stream formatting and need not reproduce source-literal grammar. Parsing rules, not visual similarity, define the contract.

sections.title: Output formatting is a separate decision
paragraphs: <iomanip> supplies setprecision. std::fixed selects fixed-point formatting and std::setprecision(2) then requests two fractional digits. The setting affects subsequent output on that stream. It changes text representation without making double exact decimal arithmetic.

Do not print prompts when the comparison contract requires only the answer. stdin already supplies input separately. Preserve exit status and exact newlines for manual checking; interface status text is not part of stdout.

sections.title: Practicum C: input and object identity
paragraphs: Read stock within 0…100, reject extra input, and create a snapshot, reference, and pointer to live stock. Issue at most three and report initial stock, remainder, and issued quantity. &alias == selected checks that both paths identify the same object without printing a numeric address.

This combines the first eleven lessons with input. It creates no new progress IDs and does not automatically push code to the cloud. Preserve source and report normally; CI execution of references is not grading a learner submission.

sections.title: Module project: units and exact rounding
paragraphs: Input m r h: m is MiB, 1024 × 1024 bytes; r is kbit/s, 1000 bits per second; h is overhead as a percentage of payload bits. Ranges are 0…1000000 MiB, 1…1000000 kbit/s, and 0…100 percent. This is a constant-rate model rather than a real-network timing promise.

num = m × 1024 × 1024 × 8 × (100+h), den = 100 × r × 1000. Round upward to seconds using num/den + (num%den != 0). The comparison produces bool, converted to 0 or 1 in the sum. Maximum num is 1677721600000000 and den at most 100000000000; long long suffices and multiplication begins with long long.

stdout contains seconds, seconds/60, and seconds%60 separated by spaces and a final newline. This ensures seconds = 60 × minutes + remainder with remainder 0…59. Invalid, incomplete, fractional, overflowing, or extra nonwhitespace input yields only invalid. Add two original cases and explain which defect they expose.

diagnostics.symptom: getline immediately returned an empty line
diagnostics.fix: Decide whether you need the current remainder or following nonblank text; ws suits only the latter constrained contract.

diagnostics.symptom: A number parsed but .5 was ignored
diagnostics.cause: The remaining input was not checked.
diagnostics.fix: After all fields consume allowed whitespace and check end of finite input.

diagnostics.symptom: A terminal run waits after Enter
diagnostics.cause: Enter is not EOF and ws may wait for more input.
diagnostics.fix: Use finite Nexus stdin or your OS’s end-of-input action; waiting is not an arithmetic error.

diagnostics.symptom: Transfer time is consistently too small
diagnostics.cause: The quotient was not rounded upward or MiB was confused with decimal units.

skills.title: Your first C++ program: from source to a verifiable report
Tokens and names: precise source with clear meaning
Comments, constants, and literals: meaning instead of magic numbers
Data types: choosing values, initialization, and measuring a target
Variables, blocks, and lifetime: a state journal
Expressions and operators: grouping, values, and clear steps
Arithmetic and assignment: quotient, remainder, and safe intermediates
Type conversions: intent, information loss, and range checks

requirements: Input m r h with the theory’s ranges: exactly three integer fields.
MiB=1048576 bytes and kbit/s=1000 bit/s; h is a payload-bit percentage.
All intermediate products use long long before the first multiplication.
stdout: seconds minutes remainder and newline; errors: invalid and newline.
Do not add pointers or references to the formula without a purpose; practicum C separately demonstrates that skill.
milestones: Restate units and independently derive four baseline cases.
Complete the starter calculation and stdout.
Prove the numerator upper bound and nonzero denominator.
Run 30 reference cases and two original cases.
walkthrough: 1 MiB contains 8388608 bits. At 1000 kbit/s without overhead it takes 8.388608 seconds, rounded upward to 9.
At h=25 the payload is multiplied by 125/100, producing 10.48576 seconds and rounding to 11.
num/den supplies whole seconds and a nonzero remainder adds one, avoiding a potentially risky num+den−1 sum.
At maximum volume, minimum rate, and 100% overhead, the result is 16777216000 seconds: 279620266 minutes and 40 seconds.
artifacts: main.cpp and a written unit contract.
A table of 30+2 inputs, expectations, and actual stdout.
One defect with hypothesis, repair, and repeat check.
Model limits: constant rate, specified overhead, and no real-network measurement.

assessment.question: What does cin >> value failure mean?
answers: Handle failure before using the value
assessment.explanation: Initialization does not replace extraction checks.

assessment.question: Does ws remove only one newline?
answers: No, all leading whitespace including blank lines
assessment.explanation: It does not preserve meaningful leading spaces or blank lines.

assessment.question: Why does the project reject 1 1000 0.5?
answers: A nonwhitespace .5 tail remains after integer h
assessment.explanation: Exactly three integer fields require a whole-tail check.

assessment.question: How can nonnegative num/den be rounded up when den>0?
assessment.explanation: Add one second only for a nonzero remainder.

assessment.question: What does fixed/setprecision(2) establish?
assessment.explanation: Formatting and number representation are different layers.
